newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. envoy seeks peace, Israelis, Arabs clash.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy seeks peace, Israelis, Arabs clash.

text.p: Israeli troops fired teargas and rubber bullets at Palestinians throwing stones and petrol bombs in Hebron on Friday even as U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross met leaders of the two sides to try to revive peacemaking.
Witnesses said one Palestinian was wounded by a rubber bullet.

The West Bank town's market closed down when several dozen Palestinian youths on roofs and in streets leading to a nearby Jewish settler enclave began throwing stones, petrol bombs and homemade sound bombs at Israeli troops, they said.
Minutes into the clash, several Palestinian police officers arrived and appeared to begin assessing the situation.

Israel handed 80 percent of Hebron over to Palestinian rule in January but Israeli troops remained in the heart of the town to guard fortified enclaves that house some 400 Jewish settlers amidst Hebron's 100,000 Palestinians.

Peacemaking between Israel and the Palestinian Authority broke down in March after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu sent bulldozers to carve out a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Ross seemed on Friday to have made little progress in his talks with Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat aimed at reviving the peace talks.
Israel's previous government handed most of the Gaza Strip and parts of the West Bank to Palestinian rule under a framework 1993 peace deal opposed by Netanyahu.

Netanyahu in January implemented -- after intense brokering by Ross of acrimonious Israeli-Palestinian negotiations -- the final interim handover called for in agreements signed by the government he ousted in national elections a year ago.
